answer:
Let \(p=\frac34\).

### 1. Failure restarts only its own stage
Each stage requires a geometric number of attempts with mean

\[
\frac1p=\frac43.
\]

Expected time for stage 1:

\[
3\cdot \frac43=4\text{ min}.
\]

Expected time for stage 2:

\[
5\cdot \frac43=\frac{20}{3}\text{ min}.
\]

Thus

\[
E = 4+\frac{20}{3}=\frac{32}{3}\text{ min}
=10\text{ min }40\text{ sec}.
\]

### 2. Failure restarts the entire update
A full “round” consists of attempting stage 1 and, if it succeeds, stage 2.  
The probability a round completes the whole update is

\[
\left(\frac34\right)^2=\frac{9}{16}.
\]

The expected duration of one round is

\[
3+\frac34\cdot 5
=3+\frac{15}{4}
=\frac{27}{4}\text{ min}.
\]

If \(E\) is the expected finishing time from the beginning,

\[
E=\frac{\text{expected time per round}}{\text{probability round succeeds}}
=\frac{\frac{27}{4}}{\frac{9}{16}}
=12\text{ min}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{Own-stage restart: } \frac{32}{3}\text{ min}\approx 10.67\text{ min }(10\text{ min }40\text{ sec})}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{Entire-update restart: }12\text{ min}}
\]

Equivalently: about \(10\text{ min }40\text{ sec}\) for restarting only the failed stage, and \(12\text{ min}\) for restarting the whole update.
